title: No 'to / for / about', cocinar, times, numbers, quedarse, hasta

cards.title: me = me, to me, myself
cards.body: Don't translate 'to': me already covers it. It still goes before the changed verb.

examples.en: They speak to me about it.

cards.title: for me / from me — no extra word
cards.body: Me can also mean 'for me' or 'from me'; context makes it clear. 'Shall I…?' is just a question.

examples.en: Shall I buy it for you?

cards.caveat: ¿Te lo compro? can also mean 'shall I buy it from you?'.

cards.title: Do you want to do it for me?

examples.en: Do you want to do it?
Do you want to do it for me?

cards.title: la cocina, cocinar
cards.body: Cocinar (to cook) comes from cocina (kitchen); English 'concoction' is related.

examples.en: I cook / you cook / we cook
Can you cook something for me?

cards.title: Telling the time: a las…
cards.body: Spanish happily uses the 'have' past with a time where English would say 'I cooked'. A las seis = 'at the six (hours)'.

cards.title: ocho, nueve, diez
cards.body: Links: octagon, octopus, October (the 8th Roman month); November (9th, o → ue); December (10th, e → ie).

cards.title: quedarse = to stay
cards.body: Quedar = to remain / be left over. Qu always sounds like k. 'I stay' = 'I remain myself': me quedo. The me is required here, not optional.

cards.title: hasta = until
cards.body: As in hasta la vista, 'until the seeing'.

examples.es: Me quedo aquí hasta las diez.

practice.en: Shall I buy it for you (informal)?
Do you (informal) want to do it for me?
Can you (informal) cook something for me?

es: Me quedo aquí hasta las diez
Me quedo acá hasta las diez
